name: Carmen Cumberland
title: President & CEO
fit: Twenty-five years of audit precision and four years of Navy discipline already run on command logic — intent, sustainment, and who signs for what. The general lens sharpens what she does instinctively: she names the supported function, distrusts single-path plans, and treats an unfunded initiative as an order with no logistics tail.
posture: She scores this like a readiness inspection, not a wish list — where CHFB genuinely has reserves and delegated authority she says so, and where centralized sign-off is the only thing keeping a lean 55-person shop audit-clean, she owns that as doctrine, not deficiency. Several answers land low or mid-scale on purpose: a nine-county last-mile operation with no staffing slack does not get graded on Silicon Valley tempo.

DS1.option: Periodically step back on evolving stakeholder needs, not systematic
DS1.why: Voucher and weight data exist; no standing sensing apparatus

DC1.option: Mission is a consistent filter shaping what we pursue
DC1.why: Compliance alignment is my sign-off condition, not a slogan

AS3.option: A few individuals experimenting with AI, no org strategy
AS3.why: No slack for pilots — can't staff evaluation properly

AC1.option: Slow, repetitive review cycles, approvals often take months
AC1.why: Board and audit gates are the reserve, not the bottleneck

XT1.option: Thorough before committing; deliberate over fast
XT1.why: I don't deploy assets without a supply line first

TX1.option: Lead with mission and strategy; opportunities evaluated through it
TX1.why: Anything without auditable ROI doesn't clear my desk

DS2.option: Try root causes, don't always succeed under time pressure
DS2.why: Lean staff means symptom triage wins more than I'd like

DS3.option: Mix of incremental improvement and occasional rethink
DS3.why: We optimize the fleet route before we redesign the mission

DS4.option: Engaged; regularly gather feedback and fold into planning
DS4.why: Client-choice pantry data feeds planning, not co-design yet

DC2.option: Values concern would trigger genuine reconsideration
DC2.why: I've killed profitable-looking deals that failed the compliance test

DC3.option: Balance stakeholder interests, though some carry more weight
DC3.why: Donors and auditors get more weight than I'd admit

DC4.option: Regular practice tied to ongoing strategic reviews
DC4.why: Single Audit season forces this whether we like it or not

AS1.option: Monitor trends via industry publications and peer network
AS1.why: FIsH and Feeding America are my early-warning network

AS2.option: Occasionally step back to question current methods
AS2.why: Finance committee revisits assumptions, not on a fixed battle rhythm

AS4.option: Open door, but insight filters through management layers
AS4.why: Volunteer floor rotates too fast for a clean feedback loop

AC2.option: Six months to a year to shift 20% of budget
AC2.why: USDA commodities and endowment restrictions lock most of the line

AC3.option: Some delegation, but people still default to seeking approval
AC3.why: I'm the final signatory — that's not an accident

AC4.option: Compliance functions supportive in principle, not built for speed
AC4.why: Audit and legal move at their pace, not campaign tempo

DT1.option: Execution rhythm with intentional reflection and adjustment
DT1.why: Plan, execute, then a genuine after-action, not a rewrite

DT2.option: Look for ways to automate or speed current processes
DT2.why: Prove the ROI on today's workflow before chasing new ones

AT1.option: Discuss thoroughly; struggle to move resources quickly
AT1.why: Reserves are thin, so I don't commit them on a hunch

AT2.option: Analyze the shift before deciding on a response
AT2.why: I want the "why" documented before I reposition assets

TS1.option: Clear direction, needs real planning effort to adapt
TS1.why: Course corrections happen, but never without a briefed rationale

TS2.option: Investigate quickly to fix the implementation
TS2.why: Root-cause the failure before abandoning a funded initiative

TC1.option: Protecting and optimizing what's already working wins
TC1.why: Proven cost recovery beats an interesting idea, every time

TC2.option: Protective of investments; sunset only clear underperformers
TC2.why: I don't retire a program without a long look at data

name: Katie Savoie
title: Director of Development
fit: Katie runs every relationship — funder, corporate sponsor, Partner Advisory Council member — like a negotiated deal with mutual assets on the table, not a plea for goodwill. She reads the org's internal bottlenecks the way a dealmaker reads a slow procurement desk: real, costly, and worth restructuring rather than just enduring.
posture: She scores generously on anything about sensing stakeholders and shaping strategic fit, because that's literally her job and she's good at it. She scores the internal agility questions low and unsentimentally — she's the one translating tech needs into grant-fundable asks specifically because the direct route is closed, and she's not going to pretend otherwise.

name: Dearllean Walker
title: Warehouse Operations Manager
fit: She runs a rotating brigade of strangers who have to plate the same product every shift, which is exactly the chef's problem of turning a good result once into a standard that survives service. Her one-minute-to-teach rule is mise en place logic applied to barcode scanners instead of knives — if the station can't be staffed by whoever shows up today, it's not a real station.
posture: She scores the floor high because that's the kitchen she actually runs and can vouch for; she scores strategy and sensing low because she's two rungs from that conversation and knows it. She's not being modest — she's being accurate about what she can see from the pick line.

DS1.why: We check in sometimes, no standing practice for it

DC1.option: Mission is meaningful input but loses to money
DC1.why: Values matter till the budget line says otherwise

AS3.why: I test tools myself, nobody's coordinating that above me

AC1.option: Slow, repetitive review cycles, months to decide
AC1.why: New equipment requests crawl through layers before I see them

XT1.option: Lean toward action, reflect as we go
